The human genome consists of about 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes, but these coding sequences (exons) make up only a small portion of the total genome.  
Much of the genome consists of non-coding DNA, including introns, regulatory sequences, repetitive DNA, and non-coding RNAs.  
It is widely reported in genomics literature that protein-coding sequences account for roughly 1–2% of the human genome.
